title: High-ticket categories and the web

brief.decision: Which high-ticket parent categories to show in the board pack, and how much each relies on the web

checkpoints.prompt: Write the query that answers Marieke's question.

Marieke has a follow-up. Among the parent categories you listed, what percentage of their combined net revenue came from TV & Video? Use the order lines with an order_date from 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, both days included, in the parent categories whose average net revenue per order line is above 150 euros (that average leaves out lines with a missing net_revenue_eur, and a missing net_revenue_eur adds nothing to a total). Divide the net revenue of the TV & Video lines by the net revenue of all those categories together and multiply by 100. Type the percentage with 1 decimal, for example 12.5.

model_plan: Metrics: the number of different orders, the net revenue, and the web share of that revenue as a percentage of sums (web revenue over all revenue, times 100, rounded once at the end). Output grain: one row per parent category. Table: the sales view, one row per order line. Row filter: order_date in 2025, both ends included. Group filter: the average net revenue per line above 150 euros, tested after grouping. Edge cases: lines with a missing net revenue, a category with no web lines (its share is 0.0, not missing), and orders with several lines in one category. Sort: revenue from high to low.
model_answer_template: In 2025, {n_categories} parent categories averaged more than 150 euros per order line. {top_category} led with {top_revenue} euros of net revenue from {top_orders} orders. Their web share ran from {lowest_web_pct}% to {highest_web_pct}%, so {so_what}.
follow_up_question: How did the web share of each of these categories change from 2024 to 2025?
